text: The year is seven hundred ninety-three. You are a farmer on the fjord at Kattegat. Your name is Ragnar.
The local boss is Earl Haraldson. An earl, meaning the lord of the region.
Every summer he sends his men east to raid.
What's in the east? Poor villages. And a few poorer villages.
You believe there are rich lands in the west. The Earl laughs and forbids the west.
But the west means open sea. No map, no compass.
From a traveler, you get two tools. A sun board and a sunstone.
The stone shows the sun even behind clouds. You will never lose your way.
You also need a ship. Your closest friend Floki builds it.
A bit mad, but a genius. His ship survives the ocean and can sail up rivers.
Hidden from the Earl, you set out to sea with a handful of men.
In the storm, Floki roars with laughter. You pray.
Days later, land appears. England. Before you, a monastery: Lindisfarne.
The monks have plenty of gold and no weapons. This raid will begin the Viking Age.
One monk speaks your language. His name is Athelstan.
You don't kill him. You take him along as a slave. This man will one day shake your faith.
Enough is enough. You challenge the Earl to a duel. A circle of shields forms.
Only one will leave it.
The Earl falls.
You are now the new Earl of Kattegat.
Your first act: sharing the plunder with the people.
The plague comes to Kattegat.
It takes the children first.
You hold your daughter Gyda's hand.
And the candle goes out.
Her mother lights the pyre.
All you can do is watch.
Your brother Rollo stands across the line, beside Earl Borg.
He can't raise a weapon against you.
And you can't kill him.
King Horik trusts you. And you trust him.
You are both lying.
But you lie better.
You are a king now.
Aslaug gives you another son.
You name him Ivar.
But the baby's legs are bent, his bones brittle as glass.
Aslaug holds him tight. You look away.
The weak do not live in this world. You know that better than anyone.
That night, while everyone sleeps, you take your son from his mother's arms.
The riverbank is ice cold.
You raise the blade.
One movement. That's all.
Then a tiny hand finds your finger.
It grips tight.
You can't.
You leave him there, in the mist.
But a mother always finds her child.
And that child will one day be Ivar the Boneless.
The baby his father couldn't harm will make the whole world tremble.
You carry him into the forest.
A life no bigger than your finger.
You can't.
Years later, you return to Kattegat unannounced.
Your sons are men now.
"Who wants to be king?" you ask. Nobody does.
Only Ivar welcomes you.
One day you stand beneath a giant tree. You no longer want to go on.
But ravens gnaw the rope. The gods won't let go of you.
You look for men for one last voyage. Only Ivar comes.
The storm swallows your fleet. You two are the only survivors.
Athelstan is now your closest friend.
Night after night, you talk about the gods.
You wonder about his God, he about yours.
One morning he sees a light in the water.
And he returns to his old faith.
Floki sees it as betrayal.
Athelstan doesn't flee. He finishes his prayer.
And Floki kills him.
When you return, your friend lies on the ground.
A short break.
Which character should be born next? Write in the comments.
You can't breach the walls.
So you decide to die.
Everyone comes to say goodbye at your coffin.
You hear everything.
Six unarmed men carry you into the city.
The weapons are in the coffin.
In the church, you rise.
The priests hadn't put that on the schedule.
The gates open.
And you collapse into your son's arms.
Athelstan once told you about a city. Paris.
An island in the middle of a river. Impassable stone walls around it.
The walls swallow your first assault.
You fall from the wall. Wounded, burning with fever.
If the gate won't open, make them carry you in.
You get baptized. Then you die. Or so it seems.
Your men carry your coffin into the city for a Christian funeral.
In the cathedral, the lid slides. And you rise.
The gates open. Paris falls.
On the way home, you say one thing to Floki. I know.
But victory consumes you too. A medicine from the East.
Rollo stays in Paris. He marries a Frankish princess.
Years later, you return to Paris. This time your brother stands on the walls.
And he beats you.
Born as Ragnar Lothbrok, you'd be the first Viking to sail west.
Then a king.
Then you'd take Paris, rising from your own coffin.
And it all springs from one question. What's in the west?
At night by the hearth, you tell your children stories.
You say your bloodline goes back to Odin, god of war and wisdom.
Maybe true, maybe not. But you believe it.
Your son Bjorn is twelve. Today you take him to the assembly.
He receives his first arm ring from the Earl's hand.
Now he is a Viking too. And you promise to show him the west.
With Ivar, you stand at the door of your old friend King Ecbert.
Two old kings. Both aged, both weary.
You ask one last favor. That he hand you over to King Aelle.
You send Ivar home. You whisper a task in his ear.
They'll take revenge on Ecbert, not on Aelle.
Before leaving, you hang Athelstan's cross around little Alfred's neck. It was his father's.
Then you are locked in a cage.
On the road, you see the Seer. You tell him you no longer believe in the gods.
King Aelle expects remorse from you. You give none.
They throw you into a pit full of snakes.
Your last words are for your sons. They will come, you say.
And in the sky, two ravens.
Born a farmer. Died a king.
You went west first. Your sons will follow.
So tell me. Did you write your fate, or did the gods?
You return with plunder. But the Earl seizes it all.
Because the people love you now. And that frightens the Earl.
He has your brother Rollo tortured. While you hunt, his men raid your farm.
King Horik sends you to bargain over land with Earl Borg.
Back home, a sickness awaits Kattegat.
The bargain collapses.
Borg promises your brother an earldom of his own.
Rollo is tired of living in your shadow.
The assembly forgives your brother.
In those same days, someone else arrives at your door.
Four years pass.
Aslaug gives you three sons. Ubbe, Hvitserk, Sigurd.
While you're in England, Borg burns Kattegat.
You take it back. Borg's punishment: the blood eagle.
On the night you return, Aslaug asks you to wait three nights.
You don't wait.
Horik fears living in your shadow.
He tries to win Floki to his side.
Floki tells you everything.
You return to England as a king.
King Ecbert grants you land.
Athelstan is torn between two gods.
On a journey, you meet Aslaug.
A few months later, she comes to your hall.
She carries your child.
You can have two wives, you say.
Aslaug accepts. Lagertha doesn't.
She buckles on her sword and loads her chests onto the cart.
Bjorn chooses to stay with you.
His mother kisses him and leaves.
Then Bjorn runs after the cart.
You don't stop him.
You only tell him to look after his mother.
You build a kingdom.
But you lose a family.
You let no one else take him. You carry him yourself.
To where he prayed every morning. The head of the waterfall.
You drive his cross into the earth yourself.
He was the only man who made you question your gods.
And a man of your own gods killed him.
You shave your head.
You hang his cross around your neck.
